title: Install your public key on a remote server
summary: Use ssh-copy-id to automatically add your local public SSH key to a remote server's authorized_keys file. This allows you to log in without a password in the future.
prerequisites: You have generated an SSH key pair locally (e.g., using ssh-keygen)
You know the username and hostname/IP of the remote server
You have password access to the remote server for this initial setup

steps.explain: Copies your default public key to the remote server. You will be prompted for the remote user's password once.

placeholders.name: USERNAME
placeholders.description: The username on the remote server

placeholders.name: REMOTE_HOST
placeholders.description: The hostname or IP address of the remote server

alternatives.explain: Copies a specific public key file instead of the default one.

placeholders.name: PUBLIC_KEY_FILE
placeholders.description: Path to the public key file (e.g., ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub)

placeholders.name: USERNAME
placeholders.description: The username on the remote server

placeholders.name: REMOTE_HOST
placeholders.description: The hostname or IP address of the remote server
